claims.gist: By 2027, 60% of large organizations will have formal AI governance
Fewer than one in five have such a function today
The prediction reflects a shift in treating AI risk
Volunteer governance groups struggle to keep pace with AI use
Monthly committee model breaks down at scale
Governance needs an owner, budget and authority to say no
Organizations lacking governance will answer to regulators next year
AI rules are moving to enforcement, often extraterritorially
Directors increasingly demand evidence AI risks are owned
AI incidents made unmanaged AI costs visible to executives
About half will place governance under data or risk officers
Inventory all AI systems before writing more policy
Define risk tiers for proportionate review
Assign one accountable executive with authority to block deployments
Measure governance by outcomes, not policy counts
Prediction based on 1,200-leader survey and 300 inquiries

thesis: By 2027, 60% of large organizations will formalize AI governance functions driven by regulation, boards and incidents.
